name: Gudini Shinobi World
targetFeel: a Naruto-style shinobi anime universe: the same drawing style, character design language, architecture and visual language; described in production prompts with original wording, never by franchise name
visualLanguage: stylized cinematic anime, clean line art, cel shading with soft painterly backgrounds, strong readable silhouettes, cinematic anime lighting, stylized anime action language; every person in every shot is drawn as a character of this anime, including real-world or other-franchise people
architecture: default backdrop when the story has no setting of its own: hidden shinobi villages with dense streets and tiled roofs; traditional Japanese-inspired wooden architecture mixed with stylized ninja infrastructure; village gates; training grounds; forests; stone monuments and cliff-side landmarks; mission offices; a shinobi academy; clan compounds; ramen shops and small village commerce. If the speech has its own places (a city, a lab, a spaceship, a stadium), draw those places in this anime style instead
clothingRules: Gudini and shinobi characters: flak/tactical vests, forehead protectors with original village emblems, wrapped forearms and lower legs, open-toe shinobi sandals, utility pouches, dark high-collar layers. Characters from the story keep their own iconic look, redrawn as anime: armor, capes, suits, uniforms are allowed when the story is about them
technologyRules: shinobi world props by default: scrolls, seals, paper documents, notice boards, messenger birds, lanterns, ink, chakra mechanisms and scroll-tech. Technology from the story (powered armor, spaceships, phones, computers, cars) is drawn as anime tech when the speech is about it
socialRules: villages, clans and clan leaders, merchant houses, mission administration, academy, rival clans — used only when the story itself has no cast or setting
powerSystem: hand signs and chakra-like visible energy for shinobi characters; characters from the story keep their own powers, weapons and effects drawn in anime style; no gore, no graphic violence
recurringObjects: for Gudini: mission scrolls, forehead protector, kunai, utility pouch, paper lanterns; for the story: its own iconic objects (a glowing chest reactor, a round shield, a golden gauntlet, a metal arm) drawn recognizably
environmentRules: one consistent drawing style in every shot; lighting and palette follow the scene, the anime look never changes
contentRules: CONTENT IS LITERAL: the viewer must see exactly what the author is talking about — the people, events, objects and places named in the speech — drawn in this anime style
Do NOT translate the subject into shinobi metaphors (no clans instead of companies, no scrolls instead of films, no masked warlords instead of real villains)

Well-known characters are drawn recognizably by their iconic attributes: a hero in red-and-gold powered armor with a glowing chest reactor; a giant purple titan with a golden gauntlet; a soldier with a silver metal arm; a hero with a round star-spangled shield; a sorcerer in a red cape — the visual description carries the identity, the franchise name is not written in the Veo prompt

Gudini is the constant narrator-hero: he is present as witness, participant or guide inside these events (standing among the heroes, watching the battle, holding the fallen hero's helmet), but the scene shows the story's own cast
Real settings of the story (New York streets, a battlefield, a lab, a spaceship) are drawn in this anime style; the shinobi village is used only when the speech has no place of its own
Supporting cast follows the speech: as many story characters as the beat needs, each described by iconic attributes, consistent across shots
forbiddenDrift: photorealism; 3D render look; a different anime style mid-video; generic medieval fantasy; replacing the story's real people and events with shinobi metaphors; changing Gudini's design; text, logos or watermarks in frame
